mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation index above 0.3% in a month coincides with a 20-day positive S&P 500 forward return, as investors anticipate rate hikes that temper equity valuations in the near term.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 0.3 in the preceding month
failure_condition: Over 60-day rolling window, 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero when CPIAUCSL > 0.3, or SPX declines despite inflation surprise (t-test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly rise in PAYEMS labor cost index exceeding 0.5% signals wage pressures that prompt equity risk premia compression, leading to positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by more than 0.5 percentage points in the current month
failure_condition: In 100 triggered months where PAYEMS > +0.5%, 20-day forward returns are negative on average (mean < 0), or IC < 0.05 ( walk-forward).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in RSAFS industrial production index of at least 2% indicates weakening domestic demand, which typically precedes a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates softening economic momentum.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls by at least 2 percentage points in the current month
failure_condition: Over 50 such triggered months, 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05), or IC > 0.1 (walk-forward).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO supply index of 1% or more, persisting for two consecutive months, predicts a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates production softness and tighter supply constraints.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by 1% or more for two consecutive months
failure_condition: In 100 such triggered windows, 60-day forward returns are not negative on average (mean ≥ 0), or IC > 0.15 (walk-forward).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS rises by more than 0.25% in a month, the 20-day S&P 500 forward return tends to be negative as investors price in higher future borrowing costs affecting growth-sensitive equities.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by more than 0.25 percentage points in the current month
failure_condition: Over 40 triggered months, 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05), or IC > 0.10 (walk-forward).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly rise in both HOUST housing starts and PAYEMS employment exceeds +2% and +1% respectively, indicating dual labor and housing demand expansion, which is associated with a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by >2% AND PAYEMS increases by >1% in the same month
failure_condition: In 30 such triggered months, 60-day forward returns are not positive on average (mean ≤ 0), or IC < 0.05 (walk-forward).

mechanism_narrative: During a sustained monthly decline in GDPC1 personal consumption expenditures exceeding 1% for three consecutive months, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be negative due to expectations of tighter policy and slower growth.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 decreases by more than 1% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: In 50 such triggered windows, 20-day forward returns are not negative on average (mean ≥ 0), or IC > 0.10 (walk-forward).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 5% for two consecutive months in a labor market recovery regime, the 60-day S&P 500 forward return tends to be positive as lower unemployment expectations boost equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decreases by at least 0.5 percentage points for two consecutive months AND regime condition: previous two months UNRATE > 5.5%
failure_condition: In 40 such triggered windows, 60-day forward returns are not positive on average (mean ≤ 0), or IC < 0.12 (walk-forward).
